findings.description: RootModel sets `__pydantic_private__ = None` as a class attribute, so the real private-attributes dict lives in the instance `__dict__`. `__copy__` shallow-copies `__dict__` and only re-copies `root`. The removed block built a new private dict, so the copy no longer aliases the original's. Without it, `copy(model)` and the original share the same `__pydantic_private__` dict. Setting a private attribute on one instance then changes the other. The removed code also dropped `PydanticUndefined` placeholders, so unset private attributes are now carried into the copy.
findings.suggestion: Restore the removed block so the copy gets its own private dict, and keep filtering out `PydanticUndefined` values. For example, `new_dict['__pydantic_private__'] = {k: v for k, v in private.items() if v is not PydanticUndefined}`.
findings.title: RootModel.__copy__ now shares the private-attributes dict with the original
